lines: Kaito
I loosened my bowstring before the others could hear it. Garrick made it sing. I thought they would laugh.
Kaito
I used to practice alone. It was easier than missing in front of someone.

options.text: Ask someone to watch a practice shot.
lines: Kaito
One person. Not an audience. If I miss, they can tell me what they saw.

options.text: Take your time. Keep practicing alone.
lines: Kaito
All right. But if I keep hiding, I will never know whether they would have helped.
Kaito
Garrick asked me to shoot while he listened. He heard a loose fitting I had mistaken for my own shaking.
Kaito
He can make the bow quieter, or leave the note in it. I have to choose what I can live with.

options.text: Choose the quiet bow. Listen carefully.
lines: Kaito
Quiet, then. I can learn to hear the road without wondering who is listening to me.

options.text: Keep the song. Try a harder job.
lines: Kaito
Then it stays. I will try tougher work with the others, instead of wondering whether I dare.
Kaito
A newcomer watched me miss the straw target. I almost told them to go away. Then they asked how to hold the string.
Kaito
I know that question. I used to save it until nobody was near.

options.text: Show them. Start with the missed shot.
lines: Kaito
I will show them what went wrong first. That is the part I wanted someone to explain.

options.text: Offer one quiet practice together.
lines: Kaito
Just us, then. That is how I would have liked to start. We can invite the others later.
Hana
I stood between the others and the trouble again. They got home, but I barely heard what they were trying to tell me.
Hana
If I am not at the front, how do I know I am protecting them?

options.text: Ask where they need you to stand.
lines: Hana
That feels like handing over my shield. No. It is asking where the shield belongs.

options.text: Keep leading. They will follow you.
lines: Hana
I can do that. I hoped you would ask me to listen, though. They are not just people behind me.
Hana
We tried the yard together. The quietest member noticed the opening before I did. I kept giving orders over them.
Hana
They stopped trying to tell me. I owe them a better answer than another order.

options.text: Apologize, then let them call the turn.
lines: Hana
I will. I can hold a position without owning every word spoken from it.

options.text: Explain the plan for a harder job.
lines: Hana
If I ask them to take on harder work, they should know why. I will leave room for an answer.
Hana
Someone asked me to walk at the back today. They said they trusted me to notice if anybody fell behind.
Hana
I never thought that could be a place of honor.

options.text: Take the rear. Keep everyone together.
lines: Hana
Then that is my place today. A shield works at either end of a group.

options.text: Ask the group where you are needed.
lines: Hana
One question before we leave. It takes less time than putting a broken plan back together.
Sora
A tired traveler asked me how to sit still. I gave them the words my teacher gave me. They only looked more tired.
Sora
Perhaps I answered the question I wanted to hear.

options.text: Ask what has been troubling them.
lines: Sora
Yes. A cup of water, and then a question. A lesson can wait for its listener.

options.text: Give them the same lesson once more.
lines: Sora
I can repeat it perfectly. I am less sure that perfection will help them tonight.
Sora
Ama let me sit beside a patient. I started to explain a breathing exercise. Ama asked whether I had heard them speak.
Sora
Their boots hurt. We loosened the laces. That was the whole lesson.

options.text: Learn to notice the small hurts first.
lines: Sora
I will start with the person, not the lesson. Ama says a comfortable bed is also good medicine.

options.text: Practice listening before you speak.
lines: Sora
One quiet breath for me, then their words. There is room for both.
Sora
The traveler came back. They showed somebody else how to loosen a boot without pulling at a sore ankle.
Sora
They did not remember my lesson. I think they remembered being listened to.

options.text: Let them teach. You can listen.
lines: Sora
I would like that. A good lesson does not need to keep my name on it.

options.text: Ask what they learned on the road.
lines: Sora
A question instead of a speech. I have been practicing. There is still plenty to learn.
Aki
My sister left a note for a new recruit: come home every time. She signed it like an order.
Aki
I used to hear that as a challenge. Now I keep counting the heads coming through the gate.

options.text: Teach them how to come home.
lines: Aki
Water, a retreat, and someone who notices you are missing. I can teach that without sounding like my sister. Mostly.

options.text: Tell them why you chose this town.
lines: Aki
Because somebody waited here. I thought I came to prove a point. Turns out I wanted a place to return to.
Ren
A carter used one of my road sketches. They marked a washed-out turn and brought it back instead of throwing it away.
Ren
There is room beside my marks for theirs. I am not sure whether to keep it tidy or keep it open.

options.text: Keep both names. Let the map grow.
lines: Ren
Both names, then. If we can tell who saw what, a correction is not a failure.

options.text: Make a clean copy; keep the old notes.
lines: Ren
A clear page for the road, and the rough one here. Nobody has to disappear to make the writing legible.
Yuna
Ama caught me giving away my supper. She put the bowl back in my hands and sat beside me until I ate.
Yuna
I want to help everybody. It is easier to say that than to admit when I need help too.

options.text: Let someone care for you tonight.
lines: Yuna
Then I will ask. Not because I have earned it. Because I am tired, and somebody is here.

options.text: Share the work, not your last meal.
lines: Yuna
I can ask the others to carry a bowl or sit with someone. Care can have more than one pair of hands.
